subject.title: Control UI: concurrent custom-group creation silently loses one group

question: Should the session-group API move to semantic atomic mutations, or retain full-catalog replacement with revision-based compare-and-set conflicts?
rationale: Both designs can prevent lost updates, but the durable Gateway protocol, ordering semantics, and client retry behavior require an explicit owner decision rather than an automated narrow patch.

options.title: Atomic semantic mutations
options.body: Add Gateway operations for add/remove/reorder that transact against authoritative rows and preserve concurrent additions.

options.title: Revisioned catalog replacement
options.body: Return a catalog revision from reads and reject stale full replacements so clients can refresh, rebase, and retry visibly.

recommendation.title: Atomic semantic mutations
recommendation.body: Add Gateway operations for add/remove/reorder that transact against authoritative rows and preserve concurrent additions.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence identifies the reporter as the only person concretely connected to the current behavior, though git-history ownership could not be established.
